description:
FILED s543b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-16) while fixing #4796.  PRE-EXISTING (base c5f618f2 = the same).  SILENT WRONG.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | PCL; scratch/s543b/p7/our.pl):
    { my $o = 2; eval 'our $o; $o = 9;'; print "1 $o ", ($main::o // "undef"), "\n"; }   # 1 2 9   | 1 9 undef
    { my $p = 2; eval 'our $p = 9; 1'; print "2 $p ", ($main::p // "undef"), "\n"; }       # 2 2 9   | 2 9 undef
    { my $q = 2; $main::q = 5; print "3 ", eval('our $q; $q'), "\n"; }                     # 3 5     | 3 2
    our $r = 1; { my $r = 2; eval 'our $r; $r = 9;'; print "4 $r $main::r\n"; }            # 4 2 9   | 4 9 1

WHAT IT IS: an `our NAME` inside a string eval, where the eval SITE has a lexical of the same name (a capture-alist key):
after the `our`, perl's NAME is the package variable (the `our` alias is a new pad entry that shadows the caller's lexical).
PCL keeps NAME a p-eval-thunk parameter bound to the caller's container, so reads and writes after the `our` go to the
caller's lexical and the package variable is never touched.

MEASUREMENT TO TAKE FIRST (cheap): `perl -I. scratch/s543b/p7/evalemit.pl 'our $o; $o = 9;' '$o'` (prints the eval
emission for capture `$o`): is `$o` in the thunk's free list although the binder resolves every use to the `our` binding
(Binder kind `our`)?  If yes, the free-name set (v1's _eval_free_vars_from_ppi walk, plus the text scan) is the place:
the BINDER is the one resolver (s543b's #4796 asks it which uses are the caller's -- Binder::uses_of of the outer binding),
so a free name the binder resolves to no outer use is not the caller's.  Not fixed in s543b: a different family (the
free-name SET, not the rename of a shared name), and the `our` lowering inside an eval thunk must then reach the package
variable through the eval's package.

WHY IT MATTERS: `our` inside eval'd code is ordinary in generated code (Exporter-style `eval "our \@ISA = ..."`,
version declarations `eval 'our $VERSION = ...'`) whenever the eval site happens to hold a lexical of that name.


=== DONE (s543k) === (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22/23; WIP 3)
Measured: `our $o; $o = 9;` with capture `$o` compiled to (lambda ($o) (p-scalar-= $o 9)) -- v1's free-name walk lists `$o` (an `our` is no lexical declaration to it) and %cap kept it.  Fix: a capture the eval TEXT declares (Binder::text_declares, now the half of shadowed_capture that asks it) is no p-eval-thunk parameter (Parser2::_assemble_eval_mode); the caller's uses already take NAME__evalcap__N (#4796), so what is left spelled NAME is the text's own -- an `our` its package's cell.
Probes (scratch/s543k/p3/probes.txt, 16 shapes: the four rows, our list, @ISA / %h, $VERSION, a nested block, package switch, use vars, own my, read before the our, twice, the cache with and without the lexical cold + warm, local our, interpolation, a sub in the eval, state, an array element): base = perl 5, tree = perl 16.  Guard eval-capture-01.t ourt_write ourt_read ourt_before ourt_version (all fail on 4a0fd0ec).
subject: SILENT WRONG: `our $o` inside a string eval whose SITE has a lexical `my $o` keeps reading and writing the caller's lexical -- `{ my $o = 2; eval q{our $o; $o = 9} }` leaves $main::o undef and sets the lexical (perl: $main::o = 9, lexical 2)
triage_reason: silent wrong: `our $o` in a string eval whose site has a lexical `my $o` (string-eval name resolution family)
